desc: Read input $N, M, Q$ and the pairs $(S_i, T_i)$ for all $M$ people.
Read queries and store them as a list of tuples `(R, L, original_index)`.
Sort the queries by $R$ in ascending order.
Implement a Segment Tree class with:
`max_B`: stores the maximum $B_u$ in the range.
`max_D`: stores the maximum $\min(A_u, B_u)$ in the range.
`lazy_A`: stores the pending range update value for $A_u$ (initially 0).
`push_up`: combines children to update parent `max_B` and `max_D`.

`range_update(l, r, val)`: sets $A_u = \max(A_u, val)$ for $u \in [l, r]$. Since we process $i$ increasingly, $A_u$ will just become $i$ if it wasn't set, but actually the logic is $A_u$ becomes the index of the *latest* person who made $u$ intermediate. So we set $A_u = i$ for the range. The value stored in node is $\min(A_u, B_u)$. When updating range $A$ to $i$, the new $\min$ is $\min(i, B_u)$. So `max_D` becomes $\min(i, \text{max\_B})$.
